I wanted a way to raise my rear wheel to do maintenance without having to buy a floor stand or a full size repair stand, so I figured out a way to do it with a cheap guitar stand that I already had lying around. It looks like this: http://img.etonals.com/p/large/MC_GS180B.jpg It also requires the bike to have a rear rack installed. This is what mine looks like: http://i5.walmartimages.com/dfw/dce07b8c-9595/k2-_372738bf-479a-4c74-940b-4a92c16e50eb.v1.jpg

What you do is unscrew the upper arm of the guitar stand and spin it around 180 degrees so the fork at the top is facing backwards. Then you extend it upwards and tighten down the adjustment bolt to hold it in place.

Next, you prop the bike's handlebars against a wall (this is to keep the front of the bike stable), and brace the front tire against something to keep the bike from rolling forward. I find that the corner of a room works well. Now lift the bike up by the back of the rear rack, then wedge the top fork of the guitar stand into the rear of the bike rack. Some guitar stands have a hinge on the fork that allows the fork to be folded down, and this could be a problem, but it doesn't fold down as long as you wedge it in the rack properly so that the downward force on the fork of the guitar stand is stopped by the end of the forks resting on top of the crossbar of the rack.

That's it. Your back wheel is now propped up and you can freely turn the crank arms to spin the rear tire for easy maintenance on the drivetrain.

I did this on a 700c road bike with a 22 inch frame, so it should also work for 29'er mountain bikes, depending on the frame size and the height of the rear rack as well as the size of the guitar stand of course. If you have smaller 26 inch rims, then this should work easily.

Other people have used rope and hooks to hang the bike, or built their own stands out of pipes from the hardware store, but I found this to be much less of a mess, and when you're done, you can return the guitar stand to its normal use.

The whole setup is pretty ghetto, but it works surprisingly well. I just used it to change my chain and tune the rear derailleur.
